content.title: Timberwolves vs. Nuggets: Prediction, How to Watch Game 2
content.text: The Minnesota Timberwolves and the Denver Nuggets face off tonight at Ball Arena in Game 2 of their 2026 NBA Playoffs Western Conference first-round series. The Timberwolves finds itself in a 0–1 hole after falling 116–105 in Game 1. Minnesota built a 10-point lead after the first quarter, but saw it erased by halftime. The Nuggets then went on a 14–0 run midway through the third quarter to take control. Still, the Timberwolves showed resilience, cutting the deficit to just two points with a little over six minutes remaining in the fourth. Denver ultimately pulled away late in a physical game that featured 42 total fouls. Jamal Murray struggled from the field (7-of-22) but still finished with 30 points, doing much of his damage at the free-throw line. The Nuggets as a team went 30-of-33 from the stripe — a decisive factor in the win. Nikola Jokić anchored the performance with a triple-double of 25 points, 13 rebounds, and 11 assists. For Minnesota, Anthony Edwards led the way with 22 points but struggled with efficiency, shooting 7-of-19, with knee inflammation perhaps a factor. To stay competitive in Game 2, the Timberwolves will need a more efficient performance from Edwards and Julius Randle, and cleaner defensive execution — particularly avoiding the kind of foul trouble that gave Denver easy points at the line. Denver’s late-game execution, ability to draw fouls, and the Jokic–Murray two-man game give them the edge at home. Final Score Prediction: Denver Nuggets 118, Minnesota Timberwolves 110 Injury Report Minnesota Timberwolves No injuries reported.
